candidate.answerReason: There are 266 positive integers below 1000 divisible by none of 2, 3 and 5. These include 1 and 165 primes, leaving 100 composites.

methods.label: Count in blocks of thirty
methods.explanation:
First count all positive integers below \(1000\) that are divisible by none of \(2,3,5\). We can then remove the primes and \(1\).

Adding \(30\) preserves divisibility by each of \(2,3,5\), so the pattern repeats in blocks of \(30\). Among \(1,2,\ldots,30\), the numbers avoiding all three divisors are exactly
\[1,7,11,13,17,19,23,29.\]
There are eight in each complete block. The integers from \(1\) through \(990\) form \(33\) complete blocks. In the remaining block from \(991\) through \(999\), only \(991\) and \(997\) qualify. Thus the count is
\[33\cdot8+2=266.\]
The disjoint blocks cover every integer from \(1\) through \(999\), so none is omitted or counted twice.

Of the \(168\) given primes, only \(2,3,5\) fail the divisibility restriction. Hence our count includes \(168-3=165\) primes. It also includes \(1\), which is neither prime nor composite. All other counted numbers are composite, so the number of prime-looking numbers is
\[266-165-1=100,\]
choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses a repeating divisibility pattern, elementary block counting and the distinction between primes, composites and 1.

methods.label: Correct for overlapping multiples
methods.explanation:
Count the integers from \(1\) through \(999\) that are divisible by none of \(2,3,5\), and then remove \(1\) and the primes.

There are \(499\) multiples of \(2\), \(333\) multiples of \(3\), and \(199\) multiples of \(5\). Subtracting all three counts removes a number twice if it is divisible by exactly two of these divisors. We restore those overlaps by adding the counts of multiples of \(6,10,15\), which are respectively \(166,99,66\).

A multiple of all three divisors is a multiple of \(30\). Such a number has now been subtracted three times and added three times, so it must be subtracted once more. There are \(33\) of them. Consequently, the number avoiding all three divisors is
\[999-(499+333+199)+(166+99+66)-33=266.\]
This adjustment leaves each allowed integer counted once and every forbidden integer counted zero times.

Exactly \(168-3=165\) primes satisfy the restriction, because the only excluded primes are \(2,3,5\). The count also includes \(1\), which is not composite. Removing these disjoint exceptions leaves
\[266-165-1=100\]
prime-looking numbers, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary three-set inclusion-exclusion, with the overlap corrections explained directly.

candidate.annotationRationale: Both methods distinguish composites from primes and 1, then obtain the desired count by removing the unwanted categories. These shared targets are captured by cnm_p157 and cnm_h010. The first method uses combined counting across repeating blocks; general inclusion-exclusion belongs only to the second method. Factors and multiples support both routes.
